# Application Auto Scaling

Store scalable targets, scaling policies and scheduled actions as configuration records without changing resource capacity.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `applicationautoscaling` |
| Signing name | `application-autoscaling` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2016-02-06` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Configuration records only |
| Selected operations | 12 of 14 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#application-auto-scaling) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- No capacity adjustments, referenced resource existence checks, IAM role creation/evaluation, CloudWatch alarms, metric evaluation, scaling activities, forecasts or runtime; omitted RoleARN uses conventional service-linked ARN metadata (EMR requires an explicit role).
- Predictive scaling and customized metric math/Metrics are excluded and reject explicitly; custom metrics support only MetricName, Namespace, Dimensions, Statistic and Unit. Predefined metric names are validated but metric-to-resource eligibility is not evaluated. Excluded member names reject with ValidationException through the existing shared AWS JSON decoder (REST JSON uses NotImplemented).
- Cron L/W/# expressions are explicitly unsupported by the shared schedule parser; actions never run. PutScheduledAction updates retain omitted members and replace supplied ScalableTargetAction/configuration objects.
- Tags apply only to scalable target ARNs, at most 50 keys; RegisterScalableTarget tags are create-only and existing targets must use TagResource.
- CloudFormation ScheduledActions, tags and undocumented ScalableTarget GetAtt attributes are excluded; removing an explicit CF RoleARN rejects (supply the desired role). Suspension omission resets false in CF; other target identity changes replace resources. CF does not implement service-specific live-state compensation beyond the shared template rollback.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
